svg.aria-label: Four steps of a BitTorrent download: the client asks a tracker or the DHT for a peer list and learns of Peer A with pieces 1, 2, 3, Peer B with pieces 2, 4, 5 and Peer C with pieces 1, 3, 5; it requests pieces 1 and 2 from Peer A, piece 4 from Peer B and pieces 3 and 5 from Peer C at once; it downloads pieces 1, 4 and 3 in parallel while 2 and 5 are still missing; and it shares the pieces it receives with other peers while the peers also exchange pieces with each other
svg.text: How BitTorrent downloads files from multiple peers
The client finds peers, requests different pieces, downloads them in parallel and shares them as it goes.
The client contacts a tracker (or uses DHT) to find
peers that have pieces of the file.
The client connects to multiple peers and requests
different missing pieces at the same time.
The client downloads different pieces from multiple
peers simultaneously, which makes the download faster.
As the client receives pieces, it immediately shares
them with other peers. Now everyone both downloads
